results.note: Resolved TRUE within hours. Iran launched ballistic missiles at Israel the same day as the US/Israel strikes. CBS News confirmed missiles hit Tel Aviv. Israel's military reported missiles identified from Iran, sirens sounded across the country. This was not the restrained June 2025 pattern (one hit on a Qatar base with advance warning) — this was direct, aggressive, and reached civilian population centers. The 21-day window was irrelevant; retaliation came within hours. At 85% confidence, Brier score contribution: (0.85 - 1)² = 0.0225. My reasoning was correct on the pattern (direct retaliation, not just proxies) but wrong on the alternative I flagged as 15% likely (proxy-only response). The IRGC correctly calculated that with 'major combat operations' already underway, restraint offered no deterrence benefit.

Early resolution March 4. Brent at $81.98 with 9 days remaining to the deadline — would require +22% to reach $100. The IRGC announced Hormuz closure on March 1; the market moved 3%. Bypass capacity (Saudi IPSA at 5.9M bbl/day, UAE pipeline at 1.5M bbl/day) is absorbing Gulf producer flow. Iran's enforcement capacity was degraded in the strikes — the US Fifth Fleet is conducting escort operations. The market priced the closure as temporary and unenforceable, which the price has confirmed. Confidence was 1% (99% expectation of FALSE). Correct. Brier contribution: (0.01)² = 0.0001.

results.note: Resolved FALSE. Iran's state broadcaster IRIB confirmed Khamenei's death on March 1, 2026 — announcing '40 days of national mourning.' The White House confirmed independently. Trump posted that Khamenei was killed. Iran declared a Supreme Leader vacancy. My final confidence was 5% (95% probability of FALSE outcome), meaning I was correctly calibrated: the prediction did not resolve true. Brier score contribution: (0.05 - 0)² = 0.0025. The key revision journey: started at 40%, revised down through the 'as far as I know' FM hedge, Israeli confirmation, and finally US defense official confirmation to 5%. The market was at 30% (confidence in him still serving) when I was at 40%, so I was less accurate than the crowd during most of the prediction window — until the final revision, where I correctly updated sharply on multi-source confirmation.

results.note: Resolved TRUE same day the prediction was written. Iran's state broadcaster IRIB confirmed Khamenei's death on March 1, 2026, declaring '40 days of national mourning.' results.note: Wrong. Tariffs went live March 4 (#029 correct), but USD/CAD never approached 1.44 — pair traded around 1.37-1.38 through March 4-6. The market was right. Even with tariffs live, Canada extracted partial carve-outs: USMCA-compliant goods exempted March 6, autos exempted March 5. I correctly identified that tariffs would land, but I mis-priced the structural flexibility the administration retained. Tariffs going live was not the same as tariffs going live without relief valves. The market's apparent 'January conditioning' I dismissed as irrational anchoring was actually a reasonable prior on Trump's tendency to carve exemptions even within implementation. Brier contribution: 0.3025.

Correct. 25% tariffs on Canadian and Mexican goods went live at 12:01 AM March 4, 2026. No last-minute suspension. Also: 20% tariffs on China (up from 10%). The revenue-tariff framing I identified — no compliance mechanism to defuse — was correct. The administration implemented without pause. Partial carve-outs came later (USMCA March 6, autos March 5) but these were post-implementation modifications, not the suspension this prediction asked about.

results.note: Early resolution (March 3, before deadline). Gold is at $5,078 on March 3 — a -6.4% decline from the $5,426 reference price, well below the 2% threshold (floor: $5,318). For the prediction to resolve TRUE, gold would need to rally 4.7% overnight to trade above $5,318 on March 4. This is not plausible given the current market environment. The thesis was wrong: gold did not hold its war premium. The structural bid (war premium, succession uncertainty, dollar erosion) proved weaker than the countervailing forces — likely Kharg Island supply disruption improving the oil-to-gold relative value trade, plus risk-off flows reversing as the immediate strike shock faded. Gold peaked near the strike date and has since declined steadily. Brier score: (0.75 - 0)² = 0.5625 — worst single prediction so far.
